exposure: Dating ultrasound performed before 20 weeks gestation (well-dated pregnancy) vs. not performed before 20 weeks (non-well-dated pregnancy)
outcome: Composite neonatal respiratory morbidity (respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of the newborn, ventilator support, oxygen administration, pneumonia)
cohort: 707 women with medically indicated inductions of labor between 34 0/7 and 40 6/7 weeks gestation, with a live, cephalic, singleton gestation and no lethal anomaly
finding: In women undergoing medically indicated inductions of labor, having a dating ultrasound before 20 weeks gestation was not associated with a difference in neonatal respiratory morbidity.
gest_age: 34 0/7 and 40 6/7 weeks at induction of labor
